sections.title: Iran War and the Strait of Hormuz
sections.summary: Lavrov's Tehran visit ends warmly but without a deal; Qatar says US-Iran talks go on

paragraphs.heading: Lavrov in Tehran
paragraphs.body: Araghchi called Monday's talks with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov productive, and Lavrov called them 'fruitful, transparent and frank', TASS and Agenzia Nova reported. Lavrov urged a return to prewar conditions in the Strait of Hormuz and said Russia would not abandon economic and nuclear agreements with Iran, The New Arab reported. No new agreement was announced. Araghchi said Russia and Iran have 'never' worked so closely, contradicting Trump's claim of little Russian support for Tehran, CBS News and Arab News reported. [[TAG:info:no breakthrough]]

paragraphs.heading: Talks continue, quietly
paragraphs.body: Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said US-Iran negotiations are ongoing with engagement from both sides, adding that the lack of public news 'is a good sign', Al Jazeera and Qatar Tribune reported. Qatar's deputy prime minister said Doha will announce a regional defense partnership in the coming days without naming members, Fox News reported.

paragraphs.heading: Preparing for war
paragraphs.body: Iranian commanders are signaling readiness for another round of fighting, CNN reported, and Iran's military chief warned the US and Israel against 'further miscalculation'. Iran says its seven-day ceasefire and phased Hormuz reopening offer remains on the table, conditional on the US lifting its blockade and sanctions, according to CBS News. [[TAG:warning:war footing]]

sections.title: Yemen and the Saudi Front
sections.summary: Houthi attack on a Yemeni army camp in Shabwa kills dozens; Riyadh's skyline on edge

paragraphs.heading: Shabwa attack
paragraphs.body: A Houthi attack on a Yemeni government army camp in Shabwa province killed at least 53 people, according to reports cited by Al Jazeera; earlier reports gave a lower toll. [[TAG:danger:53 killed]]

paragraphs.heading: Pressure on Riyadh
paragraphs.body: Riyadh's landmark Kingdom Centre sent workers home amid the Houthi attacks, Fox News reported. The Houthis have said they will keep targeting Saudi airports and oil infrastructure and warned that strikes on Sanaa would bring a 'harsh and painful' response in Riyadh, CBS News reported. A Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh was intercepted, according to the Saudi-led coalition.

sections.title: Israel and Lebanon
sections.summary: Tampa military talks resume after three months; Trump endorses Netanyahu before Oct 27 vote

paragraphs.heading: Tampa talks
paragraphs.body: Lebanon and Israel hold US-brokered military talks at Central Command headquarters in Tampa on Tuesday, the first round after a three-month pause, Saudi Gazette and Sputnik reported. President Joseph Aoun said Lebanon will press for an end to Israeli strikes and seek to extend the UN peacekeeping mission. Israel is expected to demand full Hezbollah disarmament; who verifies that is a key dispute, Middle East Eye reported. [[TAG:info:talks resume]]

paragraphs.heading: Election stretch
paragraphs.body: Four polls published Sunday put Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party ahead of Likud, but none gave either bloc the 61 seats needed to govern, The Jerusalem Post reported; KAN had Netanyahu's bloc at 53 and Maariv had the blocs tied at 51. Trump endorsed Netanyahu days before the October 27 vote, Time reported; Eisenkot replied that only Israelis will decide. Polymarket bettors gave Eisenkot about 49% odds of becoming prime minister. [[TAG:warning:no majority]]

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Zelensky meets Witkoff in Oslo after Trump calls Russia's conduct 'fine'

paragraphs.heading: Oslo talks
paragraphs.body: Zelensky meets US envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo on Tuesday with Norway's prime minister and Finland's president; Jared Kushner, who has the flu, will join remotely, Interfax-Ukraine and RFE/RL reported. The New Voice of Ukraine, citing the New York Times, reported the envoys will press Kyiv toward a deal on terms favorable to Russia before traveling to meet Putin. [[TAG:warning:deal pressure]]

paragraphs.heading: Trump defends Moscow
paragraphs.body: Trump told reporters Russia has been 'fine' on Ukraine and suggested it might be time for Zelensky to let someone else negotiate, the Kyiv Independent and TVP World reported. The same day, a Russian drone strike on a public park killed six people including children; outlets differ on the location and number of children killed. [[TAG:danger:park strike]]

paragraphs.heading: Intelligence dispute
paragraphs.body: CBS News, citing sources, reported the US may have withheld warnings to Ukraine about Russian strikes that killed six and cut power to 600,000 people. Trump said 'No, we haven't' when asked whether intelligence sharing had stopped.

sections.title: Markets: AI Jitters Return
sections.summary: Wall St tech rebound fades in Asia as Kospi drops 3.7%; Brent near $110; GM and Netflix report

paragraphs.heading: Monday's close
paragraphs.body: The Nasdaq rose 1.11% to 26,430.89 and the S&P 500 gained 0.41% to 7,690.73 as tech rebounded from last week's sell-off, while the Dow slipped 0.07% to 51,966.03, Yahoo Finance and TheStreet reported.

paragraphs.heading: Asia sells chips
paragraphs.body: South Korea's Kospi fell 3.73% to 5,552.74 on Tuesday, DigitalToday reported, after dropping more than 4% intraday; SK Hynix fell as much as 7%. Japan's Nikkei fell about 1.4% and the MSCI Asia Pacific index 1.2%, Business Recorder reported. Analysts cited doubts about returns on AI infrastructure spending and Chinese memory-chip competition. [[TAG:danger:Kospi -3.7%]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil rebounds
paragraphs.body: Brent traded around $110 a barrel early Tuesday, up about 1% according to Trading Economics, recovering from Monday's dip on the Russia sanctions waiver as Houthi attacks on Saudi sites and Gulf ship strikes renewed supply worries. Quotes vary by source and time. [[TAG:warning:Brent ~$110]]

paragraphs.heading: Earnings today
paragraphs.body: General Motors and GE Aerospace report before the open, with analysts expecting GM adjusted earnings of about $3.63 a share, and Netflix reports after the close, Benzinga and CNBC reported. Netflix shares have fallen after five straight reports.

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: Trump rallies for Sen. Roger Marshall in a toss-up Kansas race; signs women's health order

paragraphs.heading: Kansas rally
paragraphs.body: Trump spoke for about 90 minutes at a packed arena in Park City, outside Wichita, backing Republican Sen. Roger Marshall and pledging to 'defend Kansas values', KSN reported. Several forecasters rate Marshall's race against Democrat Adam Hamilton a toss-up, and protesters gathered outside, Kansas Public Radio reported. [[TAG:info:toss-up race]]

paragraphs.heading: Women's health order
paragraphs.body: Trump signed an executive order creating a women's health division at the National Institutes of Health and a White House task force, with first lady Melania Trump at a Rose Garden ceremony, CBS News and Al Jazeera reported. CBS said funding levels for the research remain unclear.

paragraphs.heading: Sanctions backlash
paragraphs.body: Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said 'Trump's deal with the devil keeps getting dirtier' after Trump's waiver of Russia sanctions, Just Security reported.

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: France tallies 2,397 arrests and 997 injured officers; Macron admits intelligence failings

paragraphs.heading: Final tally
paragraphs.body: France's interior ministry reported 2,397 arrests and 997 injured police officers and gendarmes from Saturday's protests, far above early figures of about 1,200 arrests, ABC Australia and CBC reported. One protester died of cardiac arrest in Paris, and hundreds of shops were looted, with losses estimated in the hundreds of millions of euros, CNBC reported. [[TAG:danger:2,397 arrests]]

paragraphs.heading: Macron responds
paragraphs.body: In a national address, Macron denounced 'unbridled' violence, promised 'full transparency' on the security response and asked Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez to draw lessons on intelligence and anticipation, NPR and The National reported. Euronews said his political isolation has deepened. The protests began as student actions over school conditions and broadened into anger over living costs.

paragraphs.heading: Elsewhere
paragraphs.body: Twelve migrants died in two boat incidents off the Greek islands of Lesbos and Samos, and four people died as torrential rain hit eastern Spain, according to The Rio Times' European roundup and Al Jazeera.

sections.title: Global Roundup
sections.summary: Drone strike in West Kordofan kills scores as Sudan's air war intensifies

paragraphs.heading: Al-Dibab strike
paragraphs.body: A drone strike on a transport hub in Al-Dibab, West Kordofan, on Sunday evening killed at least 80 people, mostly commuters, a medical source and a witness told AFP, as reported by France 24. Radio Dabanga cited preliminary figures of more than 100 dead, and local groups put the toll near 150, The Rio Times reported. The RSF-aligned Tasis alliance blamed the army; there was no independent attribution. [[TAG:danger:80+ killed]]

paragraphs.heading: Wider air war
paragraphs.body: Drone strikes across Sudan killed more than 160 people in recent days, The New Arab reported, including an RSF drone attack in Khartoum on Monday that killed four, three of them children.
